1.title: Exam Orientation and the Command-Line Toolkit
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and the Command-Line Toolkit. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. What the exam is. The exam environment. The speed kit. Labels and selectors. Jason Path and custom columns. A repeatable way to work every task. Practice with five hands-on labs worth eighteen points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains. Practice in this module: five labs, eighteen points, about eighteen minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero (three-node test cluster.

1.title: What the exam is
1.text: What the exam is. The figure shows this: The exam at a glance. Exam tip: The exam scores the final state of the cluster, not the commands you typed, and a task is all or nothing: check every task before you move on.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. The exam is performance-based. You get a live terminal, not multiple-choice questions. You solve real tasks on real clusters, and a script scores the final cluster state, not the commands you typed. Format. fifteen to twenty performance-based tasks in a live terminal, online proctored. Duration. two hours. Kubernetes version. version one point thirty-seven. Passing score. sixty-six percent. Price. U S D four hundred forty-five, exam only; includes one retake. Validity. two years. Simulator. killer dot S H, two attempts of thirty-six hours each, included with registration. Results. Emailed within twenty-four hours.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. Not published on the pages used for this course: how many clusters you will switch between and the exact points per task. Do not rely on a number from a blog. Read the context line of every task.

1.title: Domain weights
1.text: Domain weights. The figure shows this: Domain weights of the exam.

1.title: Domain weights, continued
1.text: Domain weights. Troubleshooting. Weight: thirty percent. Where it is taught: Modules eleven to thirteen, plus a break-and-fix task in every module. Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration. Weight: twenty-five percent. Where it is taught: Modules one to four. Services and Networking. Weight: twenty percent. Where it is taught: Modules seven to nine. Workloads and Scheduling. Weight: fifteen percent. Where it is taught: Modules five and six. Storage. Weight: ten percent. Where it is taught: Module ten. Exam focus: time goes where points are. Troubleshooting plus Architecture is fifty-five percent of the score.

1.title: The exam environment
1.text: The exam environment. You start on a host called base. Tasks name the host to use, and you reach it with S S H node. You cannot S S H from one node to another (no nested S S H). Type exit to return to base. Use sudo dash i to become root on a node. Every task begins with a context line, usually a kube control config use context... command. Run it first. Working in the wrong cluster scores zero. kube control is installed with the alias k and shell autocompletion. Also installed: yq, curl, W get, man. The Insert key is prohibited. Do not reboot base. Exam tip: Run the use context line at the top of every task first, then check the namespace and the exact names.

1.title: The exam environment, continued
1.text: The exam environment. Allowed documentation: Kubernetes dot I O or docs and the Kubernetes blog, helm dot S H or docs, gateway-api.sigs.K eights.io (C K A only), the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under slash usr slash share. The Kubernetes dot I O search is allowed. Do not open external search results. In this course's lab cluster there is no S S H. A small wrapper turns S S H C K A worker command into docker exec. Everything else (kube control, files, manifests) behaves as on the exam. Files you are asked to save go to about slash answers or on the machine where you run kube control.

1.title: The speed kit
1.text: The speed kit. Typing yamel by hand is slow. Generate it, then edit. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Generate yamel with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml instead of writing it from scratch, and use kube control explain to find a field.

1.title: The speed kit, continued
1.text: The speed kit. Pod. kube control run web the image flag set to engine X alpine the labels flag set to tier web. Deployment. kube control create deployment api the image flag set to engine X alpine the replicas flag set to three. Service for something that exists. kube control expose deployment api the port flag set to eighty. Any object as a template. add the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml. Find a field name. kube control explain pod dot spec dot containers the recursive flag or kube control explain pod dot spec then pipe to grep dash i grace. List with more columns. kube control get pods dash o wide. One value. kube control get node n one dash o json path dot status dot node Info dot kubelet Version.

1.title: The speed kit, continued
1.text: The speed kit. Loop over items. dash o json path range dot items dot metadata dot name newline end. Chosen columns. dash o custom columns N A M E dot metadata dot name,I M G dot spec dot containers zero dot image. Sort. the sort by flag set to dot metadata dot creation Timestamp. Default namespace. kube control config set context the current flag the namespace flag set to speed. Can this user do it? kube control auth can i get pods the as flag jane dash n dev. Editor: vim is the safe choice. Put set expandtab tabstop two shiftwidth two in about or dot vimrc so pasted yamel keeps its indentation.

1.title: The speed kit, continued
1.text: The speed kit. kube control explain beats searching. It shows the exact field names for the cluster version you are on, with no browser and no tab-switching. Use the recursive flag for the whole tree. Read the whole task before typing. The scoring script checks every sentence of the task. A missing label or the wrong namespace costs the full task.

1.title: Imperative first, declarative when needed
1.text: Imperative first, declarative when needed. Imperative commands ( run, create, expose, set, scale, label ) are fastest for simple objects. When a field has no flag, generate yamel with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml, edit it, and apply dash f. For a running object, kube control edit changes it in place.

1.title: Labels and selectors (they connect everything)
1.text: Labels and selectors (they connect everything). Labels are key or value tags on objects; Services, Deployments, Network Policies, affinity rules and kube control filters all find objects by label. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Labels and selectors (they connect everything), continued
1.text: Labels and selectors (they connect everything). A Service or Deployment selector that does not match the Pod template labels is a classic exam fault (Modules seven and thirteen).

1.title: JSONPath and custom columns (a frequent time-saver)
1.text: Jason Path and custom columns (a frequent time-saver). json path pulls exact values out of an object, which is how tasks such as "write the names of all nodes to a file" are solved. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: JSONPath and custom columns (a frequent time-saver), continued
1.text: Jason Path and custom columns (a frequent time-saver). dot items dot metadata dot name prints names on one line separated by spaces. range... end plus newline puts one per line. dash o name prints node or name; if the task wants the bare name, use json path or sed. custom columns prints a header unless you remove it ( the no headers flag ); check the task for "without header".

1.title: A repeatable way to work every task
1.text: A repeatable way to work every task. The figure shows this: The routine for every task. Exam tip: If you are stuck on a task after about six minutes, flag it, move on and come back at the end.

1.title: A repeatable way to work every task, continued
1.text: A repeatable way to work every task. Read the task and the context line; run the use context command. Note the namespace and the names given. Use them exactly. Do the task with the fastest command. Verify with one command ( kube control get, kube control describe, kube control logs, curl ). A task that "should" work and does not is the most common loss. If a task is stuck after about six minutes, flag it, move on, and return at the end.

2.title: Lab 0.1: jsonpath nodes
2.text: Lab zero point one: json path nodes. This task is worth three points, and you should plan about three minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Save the names of all nodes, one name per line, sorted alphabetically and without a header line, to about slash answers slash nodes dot txt on the host where you run kube control (the exam's base host). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 0.1: jsonpath nodes, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get nodes dash o json path range dot items dot metadata dot name newline end sort about slash answers slash nodes dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash nodes dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 0.2: dry run yaml
2.text: Lab zero point two: dry run yaml. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create the namespace speed. Generate (do not hand-write) a Pod manifest for a Pod named probe with image engine X alpine and the label tier web, and save it to about slash answers slash pod dot yaml. Then create the Pod from that file in the namespace speed. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 0.2: dry run yaml, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create ns speed. Then kube control dash n speed run probe the image flag set to engine X alpine the labels flag set to tier web the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml about slash, and so on. Then kube control apply dash f about slash answers slash pod dot yaml dash n speed. Then kube control dash n speed wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash probe the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 0.3: explain field
2.text: Lab zero point three: explain field. This task is worth three points, and you should plan about three minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Without opening a browser, use kube control explain to find the name of the Pod spec field that sets how many seconds a Pod gets to shut down gracefully after it is told to stop. Write only the field name to about slash answers slash field dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 0.3: explain field, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control explain pod dot spec then pipe to grep dash i grace. Then echo termination Grace Period Seconds about slash answers slash field dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 0.4: default namespace
2.text: Lab zero point four: default namespace. This task is worth three points, and you should plan about three minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create the namespace speed. Change the current context so that kube control uses speed as its default namespace, without editing any file by hand and without changing the context name. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 0.4: default namespace, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create ns speed. Then kube control config set context the current flag the namespace flag set to speed. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 0.5: labels selectors
2.text: Lab zero point five: labels selectors. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace lbl, three Pods exist: p one, p two and p three, each with the label env dev. Change the label env of p one and p two to prod (do not recreate them). Write the names of all Pods with env prod, one per line and sorted, to about slash answers slash prod dot txt on the host, using a label selector. Then delete all Pods that still have env dev using a label selector (not by name). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 0.5: labels selectors, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n lbl label pod p one p two env prod the overwrite flag. Then kube control dash n lbl get pods the show labels flag. Then kube control dash n lbl get pods dash l env prod dash o name sed s pod or sort about slash answers slash prod dot txt. Then kube control dash n lbl delete pods dash l env dev. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does the exam score: the commands you typed or the final cluster state? Answer: The final cluster state. Question two. What is the first action on every task? Answer: Run the context line (the kube control config use context command) given in the task. Question three. Which domain carries the highest weight, and what is the weight? Answer: Troubleshooting, thirty percent.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the passing score and how long is the exam? Answer: sixty-six percent and two hours. Question five. How do you reach another host on the exam, and can you S S H from one node to another? Answer: With S S H node from base; nested S S H is not allowed, so type exit first. Question six. Which command shows the exact name of a Pod spec field for the cluster you are on? Answer: kube control explain pod dot spec (add the recursive flag for the whole tree).

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. How do you generate a Pod manifest without creating the Pod? Answer: Add the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml to kube control run. Question eight. Which websites may you open during the exam? Answer: Kubernetes dot I O docs and blog, helm dot S H or docs, gateway-api.sigs.K eights.io, and the Quick Reference links in the exam; not external search results.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Score: sixty-six percent to pass; two hours; fifteen to twenty tasks; state is scored. Weights: Troubleshooting thirty, Architecture twenty-five, Networking twenty, Workloads fifteen, Storage ten. Start of every task: use context, namespace, exact names. Generate yamel: the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml. Find fields: kube control explain... the recursive flag. Output control: dash o json path, dash o custom columns, the sort by flag, dash o wide. Hosts: S S H node, sudo dash i, exit; no nested S S H. Stuck for six minutes: flag it, move on. In the next module, we continue the course.
